sections.heading: Function
paragraphs: PRKCA is responsible for converting 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), which is responsible for initiating active DNA demethylation [Ketchum et al., 2024].

paragraphs.text: Our cohort analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that PRKCA is disturbed as shown here.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: When PRKCA is compromised, downstream signaling required for neural crest cell differentiation and pharyngeal cartilage formation is impaired, which can lead to craniofacial malformations like cleft lip and palate [Chen et al., 2023, Wang et al., 2024].

paragraphs.text: Our analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that demonstrates the oligogenic interaction involving PRKCA.
paragraphs.suffix: to see the co-occurring SVs that are appearing with PRKCA in our curated palatogenesis pathway diagram. It shows the involvement of developmental enhancers via the TET-SNAIL4-BMP axis.
